title: Key Remapping in Mapped Types knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a mapped type?
options: To map a URL to a server without configuration.
To convert TypeScript to a database schema automatically.
To transform properties by iterating over keys of an existing type.
To loop over object properties at runtime.
questions.answer_key: To transform properties by iterating over keys of an existing type.
questions.explanation: Mapped types derive related type shapes and can modify property names or modifiers.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Key Remapping in Mapped Types”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with renaming properties and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with renaming properties and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Renaming properties”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Key Remapping in Mapped Types”?

Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check filtering keys with conditional types, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
